clue.text: Invent cosmetics?

definitions.meaning: to invent a story is to concoct or fabricate it
lipstick, powder and the like, the stuff applied to the face

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means fabricate, and the compound noun names facial cosmetics: one spelling, two senses.

clue.text: See 22
West dear to Boar's Head district?

parts.note: the opposite of west is east
the opposite of dear, meaning expensive, is cheap

explanation.surface: An actor called West fond of a pub named the Boar's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is the opposite of its clue word, an Araucaria liberty. The Boar's Head was Falstaff's tavern in Shakespeare, in this City of London street.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastcheap is the London street where the Boar's Head Tavern of Shakespeare's Henry IV plays stood.

clue.text: Quietly spoken cockney exclamation sounding aristocratic?

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
lummy is the cockney cry of surprise, as in 'cor lummy'

explanation.surface: A soft cockney oath that oddly sounds upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London dialect, so its exclamation sitting inside a posh word is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A plummy voice is rich and affected, the accent of the British upper classes.

clue.text: Woodcock willing to go to prison?

parts.note: game means ready and willing, as in 'I'm game'
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: A woodcock apparently volunteering to go to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' simply joins the two pieces. BIRD for time in prison is British slang, from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' for 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a wading bird shot for sport, an example of quarry hunted by guns.

clue.text: See 6
Union movement infiltrated by noisy fellow with audible advice, now 26

indicators.note: the fellow piece gets inside the pair of words before it

parts.note: marriage is a union of two people
a dance is a rhythmic movement

indicators.note: noisy means the word is heard rather than spelt, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: guy means a fellow or man

indicators.note: audible means a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: counsel means advice

explanation.surface: A trade union march is gatecrashed by a loud man shouting tips, now that relating is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union movement' reads as trade unionism, but it is a wedding dance; 'noisy' and 'audible' each signal a sound-alike. The British marriage counselling charity renamed itself in 1988 to the answer at 26.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marriage Guidance Council was the former name of the British counselling charity now called Relate.

clue.text: Painter essayist successfully brought home?

definitions.meaning: Francis ... was a twentieth-century Irish-born British painter
Francis ... the Elizabethan philosopher wrote famous essays
to bring home the ... means to succeed or earn a living

explanation.definitionFit: Two famous Francis Bacons, painter and essayist, plus the idiom 'bring home the bacon' meaning succeed.

clue.text: Withdrawal in case of pull

parts.note: re means in the matter of, as in legal case headings
traction is the act of pulling

explanation.surface: A retreat made in the event of a tug.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is the withdrawing of a statement or the drawing back of something.

clue.text: See 13
Repeat summons to speak in public

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, so a repeat is signalled by it
to cite is to summon someone to appear in court

explanation.surface: An instruction to call someone again to address an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as RE-CITE, 'summon again', which is how Araucaria intends 'Repeat summons'.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim a poem or passage aloud before an audience is to give a public recitation of it.

clue.text: Staircase on board in style of value in 6?

indicators.note: a style of something reverses the order, putting the companion word before the way

parts.note: clue 6 is the marriage counselling body, and companionship is a value prized in a marriage
way means manner or style, as in 'in the way of'

explanation.surface: A ship's stair described as in keeping with what a marriage values.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 6, the old name of the marriage counselling service, where a partner is a companion; 'the style of a companion' is a companion's way.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the stairway leading from deck to cabins below is called by this nautical term.

clue.text: Express congratulations permitted in performance with energy

indicators.note: the permitted word sits inside the performance word

parts.note: a feat is an accomplishment or performance
licit means lawful or permitted
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Offering praise for an allowed show full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' suggests a show, but here it means an accomplishment; 'in' signals the insertion, and 'with' simply adds the energy symbol at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To felicitate someone is a formal way to congratulate them.

clue.text: A certain something from Jaques — 1 is one

indicators.note: the letters are made out of the words that follow, rearranged into new order

parts.note: 1 here is taken as the Roman numeral I rather than a cross-reference

explanation.surface: Jaques, the melancholy courtier of As You Like It, supplies an indefinable quality, and makeup at 1-across is one.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to MAKEUP, and the surface invites that reading, but it is the Roman I; rearrange JAQUES, I, IS and ONE to get the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally 'I don't know what' means an indefinable appealing quality, a certain something.

clue.text: Think of a tooth: it took food

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
ate means took food

explanation.surface: Someone musing about a tooth that ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder, a formal synonym of meditating.

clue.text: Temptations to guide for international

definitions.meaning: both words of the phrase can mean a temptation or ordeal, as in the 'time of trial'
a match played to select or prepare players for a Test, the international match in cricket

explanation.definitionFit: Test and trial both mean temptation; the phrase also names a match that guides selection for a Test.

clue.text: Potterne building used as warehouse

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A building in the Wiltshire village of Potterne is used for storage.
explanation.walkthrough: Potterne is a village in Wiltshire, England; 'building' turns it into new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading port or depot where goods are stored, a warehouse.

clue.text: Latino in fear of Latino?

parts.note: belonging to the Latino man is his
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: A Latino man in a state of terror about another Latino.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in the split: a Latino man's fright belongs to him, so 'fear of Latino' is the possessive pronoun plus the fear word. Joining them in that order gives the definition's own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic describes a person of Spanish-speaking, often Latin American, descent, which is what Latino means.

clue.text: A lot of white against one in colour has a certain cachet

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: snow is the white stuff

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes inside the colour word

parts.note: blue is a colour
v is short for versus, meaning against
a means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A rich expanse of white set against a single hue gives a certain distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' means most of the word, dropping its last letter (SNO); 'in' puts the versus abbreviation and one inside the colour, giving BVALUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snob value is the appeal something has from its prestige or exclusiveness, its social cachet.

clue.text: Star of the upper atmosphere?

parts.note: alt means high, as in the musical term for high notes
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A star found high in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Magical remedy for somewhat sick part of speech from the right — let us know about it

indicators.note: the reversed phrase is wrapped around the two further pieces
reading from the right means the words are taken backwards

parts.note: let us know is a paraphrase of tell us

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: ill means sick
a verb is one of the parts of speech in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone sickly is promised a miracle cure if they share what they know about a word class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the right' turns the paraphrase backwards (SULLET); 'somewhat' keeps only part of the sickness word (IL); 'about' wraps the reversed phrase round ILVERB. 'it' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver bullet, in folklore the only weapon to kill a werewolf, figuratively means a simple magical cure for a problem.

clue.text: See 18
Left London for Washington in flower

parts.note: the great wen was William Cobbett's name for London

indicators.note: the state abbreviation goes inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, here the Scottish river Tay
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Someone quit London for Washington DC in blossom time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, not a bloom, and the great wen is an old nickname for London coined by Cobbett; 'in' signals the insertion, giving TAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gone away is to have left, the past tense of departing.

clue.text: Mural piece to beat

parts.note: mural means of a wall, so it stands for wall
op is short for opus, a musical piece

explanation.surface: Part of a wall painting is used to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallop is to hit hard or thrash, a colloquial verb meaning beat.

clue.text: Pipe of wine retaining its heart

indicators.note: the wine word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
its refers to wine, whose central letters are I and N

explanation.surface: A pipe of wine, the large cask, keeping its core.
explanation.walkthrough: A pipe is also a large wine cask, which the surface leans on; 'its heart' means the heart of 'wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, and pipe is a general word for any tubular wind instrument.

clue.text: Ring round a lot of lots to get place of honour

indicators.note: the ring word goes round the trimmed piece

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, here a large part kept

parts.note: lots are fates or destinies

explanation.surface: Bells chime around much of an auction to secure a seat of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' are fates, as in 'cast one's lot'; 'a lot of' keeps only the first four letters (DEST), and 'round' places them inside the bell-ringing word.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone on a pedestal is to place them in a position of admiration; the base for a statue gives the idiom.

clue.text: Give an account about the deceased?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
late means dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: Telling a story concerning someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to narrate or tell, giving an account of events. It is also the current name of the counselling body at 6.
